sub: Named after the sky “splitting open” (inshaqqat) in ayah 1
theme: The Resurrection and the reckoning. Sky and earth obey Allah without question; man is toiling toward Him and will meet his deeds, in his right hand or behind his back.
story: Revealed in Makkah, among the earliest surahs. Persecution had not started yet, but the message was openly rejected, and people refused to believe they would be raised and made to answer for their deeds.
The surah answers that denial. Sky and earth obey their Lord at once. Man is on a journey to meet Him, and will receive his record either in his right hand or behind his back.
The Prophet ﷺ prostrated when he recited this surah. A companion who prayed behind him said he would never stop prostrating in it until he met him.

sections.title: When the sky splits and earth empties itself, both obey their Lord
sections.meaning: On the Last Day the sky splits open, and the earth is stretched flat and throws out everything inside it. Both simply listen to their Lord and obey, as they must.
points: The sky splits, listening to its Lord
The earth is stretched flat and empties itself
It too listens and obeys, as it must
sections.matters: The surah opens with the end of the world, but the point is obedience. Sky and earth never argue with Allah’s command. Man, who was given a choice, is shown what submission looks like.
sections.story: No specific incident. It answers the people of Makkah who denied the resurrection.
explained: Idhā, “when”, opens a chain of events on the Day of Judgement. The sky tears apart. Adhinat li-rabbihā: it hears its Lord’s command and obeys. Ḥuqqat: that is only right, because nothing can resist His command.

The earth is stretched out like leather, with no mountains or buildings left, wide enough for everyone gathered. It throws out the dead and its treasures and becomes empty. What happens next is left unsaid; the next ayah supplies it: man meets what he did.
teaches: Obey Allah’s command the way the sky and earth do: without delay.
The earth will give back everything it holds.
The Day of Judgement is certain, and it begins with huge change.
sections.hook: Ayat 2 and 5 end with the same words, wa-adhinat li-rabbihā wa-ḥuqqat: once for the sky, once for the earth. Two “when” (idhā) openings, at 1 and 3.

sections.title: Record in the right hand brings joy; behind the back, the Blaze
sections.meaning: Every person is toiling toward his Lord and will meet Him. Whoever gets his record in his right hand has an easy account and returns to his family happy. Whoever gets it behind his back cries for destruction and burns, because he lived carefree and thought he would never return.
points: O man: you toil toward your Lord and will meet Him
Right hand: an easy account, back to family happy
Behind the back: cries for ruin, enters the Blaze
He was happy among his people, sure he’d never return
Yes! His Lord was always watching him
sections.matters: This is the heart of the surah: the journey of life ends in a meeting. It splits people into two groups and gives the reason the second group failed: carefree living and denial of the return.
sections.story: Reportedly, the right-hand ayat were revealed about Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, the first to migrate to Madinah, and the behind-the-back ayat about his brother al-Aswad. They then apply to everyone.
explained: Kādiḥ means straining hard. Good or bad, every person is working, and every step moves him toward his Lord. He will meet Him, and meet his deeds. The one given his record in his right hand gets ḥisāb yasīr: his deeds are only shown to him, not picked apart. He returns to his family delighted.

The other receives his record in his left hand, from behind his back. He cries thubūr, begging for destruction, and enters the Blaze. His crime: he was carefree among his people, following his desires, and sure he would never be brought back. Balā, yes he will: his Lord saw everything he did.
teaches: Life is effort either way; make sure yours leads somewhere good.
An easy reckoning means your deeds are shown, not interrogated.
Carefree forgetfulness of the Hereafter is dangerous.
Allah sees everything, so no one is left unaccountable.
sections.hook: Masrūr (happy) appears twice: the winner returns to his family happy (9); the loser was happy among his family (13). The section opens with a call: yā ayyuhā al-insān (6).

sections.title: Life passes stage by stage, yet they won’t bow to the Quran
sections.meaning: Allah swears by the sunset glow, the night and what it gathers, and the full moon: you will pass from stage to stage. So why don’t they believe, or bow when the Quran is recited? They deny, Allah knows what they hide, and a painful punishment awaits, except for believers who do good.
points: By the twilight, the night, and the full moon
You will pass from stage to stage
Why don’t they believe, or bow to the Quran?
They deny; Allah knows what they hide
Painful punishment, except believers: an unending reward
sections.matters: The oaths show that nothing stays the same: day turns to night, the moon grows full. Man also moves through stages toward his Lord. After such signs, refusing to believe has no excuse.
sections.story: No specific incident for most of it. One report says ayah 22 was about four men of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr, two of whom later accepted Islam; others take it as all disbelievers.
explained: Allah swears by three things that change: ash-shafaq, the red glow after sunset; the night, which gathers everyone home; and the moon as it fills into a full moon. The oath: ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaq, you will move from one stage to the next, from birth to old age, death, resurrection and judgement.

So what is stopping them? When the Quran is recited, they do not bow in submission. They simply deny, and Allah knows the denial and the deeds they gather inside. Give them news of a painful punishment. Those who believe in their hearts and act with their limbs have a reward that never ends.
teaches: Your state will keep changing, so prepare for the final stage.
When the Quran is recited, let your heart submit.
Allah knows what people hide, not just what they show.
Faith needs deeds; together they earn a reward without end.
sections.hook: Three oaths (16–18) lead to one sworn line (19). Ayah 21 carries the sajdah mark. Like section 2, it ends with two groups: deniers (22–24), then believers (25).

groups.text: The sky splits apart, listening to its Lord and obeying, as it must.
The earth is stretched flat, throws out what it holds, and also obeys.
O man, you are straining toward your Lord, and you will meet Him.
Whoever gets his record in his right hand has an easy account and returns to his family happy.
Whoever gets it behind his back cries for destruction and burns in the Blaze.
He was carefree among his people, sure he would never return. But his Lord saw him.
By the sunset glow, the night and the full moon: you will pass stage after stage.
Why don’t they believe, or bow when the Quran is recited?
The disbelievers deny, and Allah knows what they hide.
A painful punishment for them; an unending reward for believers who do good.

1.explain: Inshaqqat: the sky tears open on the Day of Judgement, its parts separating and its stars scattered.

2.explain: Adhinat li-rabbihā: it listens to its Lord’s command to split, and obeys. Ḥuqqat: and it must, since His command cannot be refused or overcome.

3.explain: Muddat: the earth is stretched out like leather, its mountains and buildings levelled, until it is wide enough to hold everyone gathered.

4.explain: It throws out what is inside it, the dead and its buried treasures, and becomes completely empty.

5.explain: The earth too listens and obeys, as it must. The “when…” sentence is left open; what follows fills it in: man meets what he did.

6.explain: Kādiḥ: straining with effort. Every person is working his way to his Lord, with good or bad, and will meet it: meet his Lord, and meet his deeds.

7.explain: Given his record of deeds in his right hand: the believer, one of the people of happiness.

8.explain: Ḥisāb yasīr: an easy account. The Prophet ﷺ explained that this is only the presentation of deeds; whoever is questioned in detail is punished.

9.explain: He returns to his family masrūr, delighted: either to his family in Paradise, or to his family from this world, to share the good news.
9.why: Reportedly revealed about Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, the first to migrate from Makkah to Madinah. It then applies to every believer.

10.explain: Given his record behind his back: in his left hand, reached from behind him. This is the disbeliever.
10.why: Reportedly revealed about al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, Abū Salamah’s brother. Like ayah 9, it then applies to everyone.

11.explain: Yadʿū thubūrā: when he reads his record, he calls out for destruction, “O my ruin!”, wishing death would end it.

12.explain: He enters the Saʿīr, the blazing Fire, which surrounds him on every side.

13.explain: In the world he was happy among his people, following his desires and never thinking of what lay ahead. Believers, by contrast, lived among their families in awe of Allah (52:26).

14.explain: Lan yaḥūr: he was sure he would never return to Allah, never be raised after death.

15.explain: Balā: yes, he will! His Lord saw him from the day He created him, and would never leave him without command, reward or punishment.

16.explain: Fa-lā uqsimu: so I swear. Ash-shafaq: the red glow on the horizon after sunset, the start of the night. Some say the whiteness after it.

17.explain: Wa mā wasaq: and what the night gathers. At night everything that spread out by day goes home: people, animals and birds.

18.explain: Ittasaq: when the moon gathers its light and becomes full, in the middle nights of the month.

19.explain: Ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaq: stage after stage. From fluid to child, youth to old age, death, resurrection and judgement; or hardship after ease, and ease after hardship.

20.explain: Fa-mā lahum: what is stopping them from believing, when the proofs are this clear?

21.explain: When the Quran is recited, they do not bow in submission. The Prophet ﷺ prostrated when reciting this surah, and a prostration of recitation is made at this ayah.

22.explain: Bal: rather, stubbornly denying the truth after it is clear is their habit, so their unbelief is no surprise.
22.why: Reportedly revealed about four men of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr, two of whom accepted Islam. Others take it as all disbelievers.

23.explain: Yūʿūn: what they gather and hide in their chests, denial and evil deeds. Allah knows all of it.

24.explain: Bashshirhum: give them tidings. The word is used for news that shows on the face, joy or grief; here it is a painful punishment.

25.explain: Except those who believe in their hearts and act with their limbs. Ajrun ghayru mamnūn: a reward never cut off and never reduced.
